The strong weighting toward 24–25°C captures the narrow uncertainty band in these short-range forecasts, while the minimal odds on 26°C+ or sub-23°C reflect the low likelihood of significant deviations from current steering patterns or intensification. **Official forecasts from the National Weather Service and other sources point to a high in the mid-to-upper 70s°F for Chicago on August 25, 2026, with some models and inland areas reaching the lower 80s.** NWS point forecasts list a high near 75–76°F under mostly sunny skies, while broader guidance and private services such as WeatherBug cite 78°F, noting lower-80s readings away from the immediate lakeshore and mid-70s right along Lake Michigan. These values sit close to the long-term August 25 average high of ~82°F but reflect a cooler air mass following yesterday’s 78°F maximum at O’Hare.

Light southerly to southwesterly winds are expected to limit strong lake-effect cooling during peak heating hours, while clear skies and modest dew points support efficient daytime warming. Historical analogs and climatological baselines favor readings in the upper 70s to low 80s when high pressure dominates late August. The market-implied probabilities—64% for 80–81°F and 26% for 78–79°F—therefore track the upper end of the forecast envelope that traders are weighting most heavily, consistent with the spread between official NWS guidance and slightly warmer model blends or inland observations. No major forecast shifts have occurred in the past 24 hours that would materially alter this range.

Model consensus and recent observations show little deviation from this range, with only modest upside risk if the marine layer erodes earlier than expected.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the German Weather Service (DWD), ECMWF ensembles, Met Office, and BBC Weather indicate a daytime maximum of 25–27 °C in Munich on August 26, 2026, under mostly cloudy to overcast skies with possible early showers and light southerly or variable winds. These conditions limit surface heating and align with the market’s leading outcomes at 26 °C (41.5 %), 25 °C (22.5 %), and 27 °C (21.5 %). Late-August climatology shows average highs near 23 °C, so the current setup reflects a modest positive anomaly without the strong high-pressure ridge or clear skies needed for 28 °C or higher. Model spread remains narrow, with ensemble members clustering in the mid-20s; any last-minute clearing or reduced cloud cover could nudge the official reading (from Munich Airport or DWD stations) toward 27 °C, while persistent showers would favor 25 °C. Updated high-resolution runs and afternoon observations will be the key near-term drivers.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast consensus from multiple models points to a mild winter day in Buenos Aires on August 26, 2026, with the highest temperature most likely reaching 18–20°C.** Northeasterly winds are advecting warmer maritime air ahead of a frontal system, supporting daytime maxima several degrees above recent averages of 13–14°C. Current observations on August 25 show highs near 13–14°C under mostly cloudy skies, with the pattern shifting to partly cloudy conditions and lighter winds that favor greater solar heating. Official agencies including Argentina’s SMN and international guidance (GFS/ECMWF analogs) show tight clustering around 16–19°C, though variable cloud cover and exact frontal timing introduce modest uncertainty. Traders assign the highest implied probability (41%) to 19°C, reflecting this consensus while pricing in a small chance of 20°C or higher if clearing occurs earlier than expected. New model runs and the official maximum observation tomorrow will resolve the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from Mexico’s Servicio Meteorológico Nacional project a daytime maximum of 23–25 °C for Mexico City on August 26, 2026, under partly to mostly cloudy skies with scattered showers and variable winds of 10–20 km/h. These conditions limit surface heating at the city’s ~2,240 m elevation during the peak of the rainy season, when increased cloud cover and humidity typically suppress temperatures several degrees below clear-sky potential. Ensemble model guidance shows only modest spread around this range, with afternoon convection and urban heat-island effects introducing the main uncertainty in the precise peak. Traders have therefore concentrated probability on the 24–25 °C outcomes, consistent with both climatological August averages near 24–26 °C and the latest observational trends.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from Météo-France and global models indicate a warm, humid southerly flow over Paris on August 27, with afternoon highs likely peaking near 26–28 °C amid increasing cloud cover and a 30–60% chance of thunderstorms developing late in the day. These convective developments, driven by instability and modest Atlantic influence, introduce the main uncertainty: earlier or heavier showers would suppress insolation and cap the maximum near 26 °C, while delayed or lighter activity could allow brief clearing and push readings to 28 °C. Ensemble guidance shows tight clustering around the climatological late-August baseline of ~24–25 °C but with modest positive anomalies, explaining why market-implied odds remain closely balanced among the top three outcomes and why small shifts in the next model runs or observational updates could reallocate probability.
